v11.67 - x-95: bir misyonun oturumları artık damgalı, ayrı ve tek tıkla toplanabiliyor

A mission opens a session for its planner and one for every delegation it hands
out. All of them landed in the one Sessions table, undivided, and on a farm that
runs missions they are the majority of it: the log of a person's own dialogs
became unreadable, and the other sessions could no longer be followed.

Worse, they did not even look alike. A delegation carried "launchedBy" and read
as 🤖 automation; the PLANNER has no task, no costSessionFile and runs in the
lead agent's own folder, so sessionOrigin fell through to "agentId" and filed the
orchestrator's own conversation as 🧑 a person's. That is the "some of them look
like I opened them" in the item: one mission, two glyphs, neither of them saying
which mission.

THE STAMP. SessionLauncher gains missionId + missionTitle, and publishLaunchers
now walks the mission store as well as the task ledger: the planner's own lane,
every step's runSessionId, every conversation message. A session the task walk
already named keeps its label (a delegation's own title says more than the
mission's) and is only enriched. runSessionId is the durable half — it is written
the moment a delegation binds and OUTLIVES the task row retention removes, so a
month-old mission keeps its stamp after its tasks are gone. Republished on
missionEmitter too, or the planner's lane would have waited for some unrelated
task to move.

THE THIRD GLYPH. sessionMission() is the only reader, so the table, the viewer
and the bridge cannot drift. A mission row wears 🎯 — never 🧑, never 🤖, and no
moon on it — and its hover opens with WHICH mission rather than "Automation".
`origin` is untouched: "who started it" still has exactly two answers, and this
is a different question about the same run.

OUT BY DEFAULT, AND SAYING SO. filters.missions is the same three-state shape as
agents/engines (null = no filter, so a mission started a minute ago is not
excluded by yesterday's list of ids) with the opposite default: []. It is an
exclusion, not a scope — rows that are nobody's mission are untouched by it.
Because it hides rows on a fresh panel it gets a permanent 🎯 chip beside the
origin switch, counting what it is leaving out; the Filters chip is not inflated,
for the same reason the origin scope never inflated it.

‼️ Letting them in WIDENS THE ORIGIN SCOPE with it. Every mission session is
`auto` and the table opens on 🧑 User, so the chip admitted rows the scope beside
it threw straight back out: "list them all" changed nothing on screen. Caught in
the render, not in a string test.

THE BUTTON. A run's detail header gets "🎯 Sessions" → the Sessions page scoped
to that run and nothing else (missions: [id] AND missionsOnly), with the panel
opened so the reader can see what is narrowing the list, and the mission named in
the page's own subtitle. It opens the page that already IS the right surface for
a list of sessions rather than growing a second table in the mission detail.

BRIDGE. sessions.page takes `mission` (refused on an unknown run id rather than
opening an empty page); missions.status hands back `sessions` — every lane the
run opened, each with its role, its transcript file and its own figures, gathered
off the same stamp the page filters on. parity: one new entry, gapBudget 38.

Found while wiring it: test/lib_page_dom.js only dropped its element cache on an
#app write, so a component that owns one container (the sessions table owns
#sessblock) re-wired the SAME cached element objects on every repaint and stacked
a listener each time. A control whose markup happened not to change between two
renders then fired twice per click and appeared dead — two fixtures had been
shipping screenshots of a filter panel that was never open, with every assertion
about them passing. A region rewrite now drops its own children, as a browser
does, and the sessions "filters open" pictures show a panel for the first time.
